findings.title: Redis call per key inside the loop
findings.impact: Rate-limit checks get slower as a request names more keys, and the key list comes from the client.
findings.what: One round-trip per key; 50 keys means 50 calls before the handler runs.
findings.quote: for (const k of keys) await redis.incr(k)
findings.verifier: Confirmed: `keys` comes from the request body and is unbounded (routes.ts:18).

findings.impact: Adding a limit for a new route means editing this file; plugins can't register their own.

findings.title: TTL set after increment

pack.summary: Adds per-key rate limiting in front of the batch and upload routes, backed by Redis counters with a 60-second window.

sections.title: Structure
sections.text:
- `limit.ts` is new and sits between `routes.ts` and the handlers.
- `redis.ts` gains one export, `pipeline()`.

sections.title: Call flow
sections.text: A batch request checks every key before the handler runs.
mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant R as routes.ts
  participant L as limit.ts
  participant DB as Redis
  C->>R: POST /batch
  R->>L: checkAll(keys)
  loop each key
    L->>DB: INCR key
  end
  L-->>R: ok / 429

sections.title: Building on top
sections.text:
New public API: `checkAll(keys)`, `LIMITS`, `RateLimitError`.

- To limit a new route, add it to `LIMITS` (limit.ts:12). There is no hook for plugins yet (see F002).
- No existing callers break.

sections.title: Performance
sections.text:
- Every limited request makes one Redis round-trip per key (limit.ts:44).
- Memory: one key per client per route, expiring after 60 s.
- Not measured: latency under load. A 50-key request profile would settle T1.
